key_insight: Fine-tuned transformer models, especially FLAN-T5-Large, can detect social isolation and social support cues in unstructured clinical notes with strong accuracy.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help health systems identify patients at risk of social isolation using existing EHR text and support more context-aware care.
method: Annotated clinical note spans with social context cues were used for fine-tuning.
Compared FLAN-T5-Large, BERT, RoBERTa, and Gemma-2-2B on classification performance.
Used structured prompts and included true/false positives, negations, and ambiguous terms to reduce overgeneralization.
evidence_signal: FLAN-T5-Large achieved the best Macro-F1 at 0.92 ± 0.04, outperforming Gemma-2-2B (0.89 ± 0.10), RoBERTa (0.80 ± 0.21), and BERT (0.77 ± 0.17).
watch_item: Performance was evaluated on annotated notes, so real-world deployment may face domain shift, variable documentation quality, and the need for careful validation to avoid false positives.
paper_title: Fine-Tuned Large Language Models for Detecting Social Isolation from Unstructured Clinical Notes
